chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not bury your dead one in the grave, but place him away from it by two cubits or three, and leave him to prepare himself.'

key_terms.أُهْبَتَهُ: his preparation / his state of readiness

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method for placing the deceased in relation to the grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises placing the deceased beside the grave pit rather than directly within it, allowing the body to 'prepare' (take its *uhba*) before final interment, a practice reflecting the Shia emphasis on dignified and gradual burial rites. This specific etiquette underscores the reverence for the dead, distinguishing the preparation phase from the final resting place, and is recorded in *Al-Kafi* as a practical guideline for funeral conduct.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Muhammad Bin Ajlan who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not offload your dead one in the grave, but place him away from it by two cubits or three, and leave it to prepare himself’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Muhammad ibn ‘Ajlan who has said the following: “

Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘You must not make it heavy for your deceased by placing him in the grave. Place him two or three yards away from the grave on the ground so that he can get ready.”’
